written: 2026-09-29, before any showcase session, any card learned on these families, or any detection score on their prompts
question: What does the SHIPPED product (hooks installed as `adage init` installs them, the background learner `adage condition --auto`, procedure cards delivered by hook, uplift gating) do to the cost, speed and pass rate of recurring developer tasks, across 5 families on 5 repositories, when it learns each family from 4 ordinary sessions of the user's history with no harness intervention? Publishable numbers for the website: pooled and per family, with intervals, n, spend and caveats.

design.model: claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 (primary), Claude Code as installed, version recorded per session
design.runner: evals/live/runner.py through the GO validation's gv_run.py (imported unchanged by sc_run.py): --host-auth, confine: true (bubblewrap), isolated HOME per session, tools pinned, max_turns 60, concurrency 2, CLAUDECODE and CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID never forwarded
design.training: per family, 4 sessions, sequential, the product installed (adage hooks-config), ADAGE_HOME persistent, nothing else set: the product's own background learner forms the family and compiles the card after each session; the driver waits for the learner before the next session; the runner's learn phase is refused
design.held_out: per family, 8 variants x 2 repeats x {control, adage}, arm order seeded per (variant, repeat) with seed 20260929, paired by (variant, repeat), learning frozen (ADAGE_AUTO_LEARN=0) so every pair sees the index learned from the 4 training sessions

arms.control: hooks installed, directives (cards included) computed and logged, not delivered (ADAGE_ARM=control)

sonnet_arm.variants: the first 6 held-out variants of each family, in the order above
sonnet_arm.index: a copy of the family's Haiku-learned ADAGE_HOME (no Sonnet training): the same card, a stronger model
sonnet_arm.why_these_families: the two cheapest families (expected $/session), one Python and one Go, one ported and one new

design.identical_to_go_validation: training as a user, learner wait, frozen held-out index, arms, pairing, seeding, isolation, turn cap and runner are the GO validation's (evals/launch/go-validation), reused unchanged
deviations_from_a_pure_user_flow: learning is frozen during held-out sessions (a user's index would keep learning from them)
the driver waits for the learner between training sessions
the Sonnet arm reuses the Haiku-learned index (a Sonnet user would have Sonnet-learned cards)
prompts follow one template per family (the shipped detector is strict: 0/6 informal paraphrases were recognised in the Go research family); paraphrase recall is out of scope

stages.A: training, all 5 families (20 sessions), then sc_detect.py per family ($0 probe: card formed, held-out delivery, false fires on 6 negatives)
stages.B: held out, repeat 1, all 5 families (80 sessions), then the interim harm check R4
stages.C: held out, repeat 2, all 5 families (80 sessions)
stages.D: the Sonnet arm (24 sessions), only with budget left (R6)
stages.order_rationale: every family's repeat 1 before any repeat 2, Sonnet last: if the global cap binds, it costs repeats or the Sonnet arm, never whole families

metrics.primary: $/task, Claude Haiku 4.5, INTENTION TO TREAT over every held-out pair of the 5 families (detection misses included): billed total_cost_usd per session; adage/control - 1 as the ratio of the pooled paired sums (sessions of pricier families weigh more, as dollars do); 90% CI

secondary.calls: tool calls per session, same estimator
secondary.wall_time: wall-clock seconds per session (runner `elapsed`), same estimator; the machine is shared, so read it with the caveat
secondary.pass_rate: hidden check per arm (Wilson 90%) and the paired difference adage - control (same bootstrap)
secondary.card_delivery_rate: share of adage held-out sessions whose spool records a card delivered (route card-..., kind directives), Wilson 90%
secondary.false_fires: cards delivered to the 30 same-repository negative prompts (6 per family: 3 RepoBench one-off fixes whose real fix edits the family's files, 3 hard negatives) in the $0 probe through the installed hook after training, at the prompt OR at the first edit of a card file (both count); Wilson 90% upper bound; the prompt/edit split is reported

metrics.per_family: every primary and secondary metric within each family (8 variant clusters, 16 pairs)
metrics.sonnet: the same contrasts for the Sonnet arm, per family (6 pairs) and pooled (12 pairs): directional only
diagnostic: sensitivity: the primary without pairs where either session hit the 60-turn cap
the primary restricted to the variants the $0 probe delivered the card for (a pre-treatment subset, fixed before any held-out session)

analysis.code: analyze.py (render.py turns its output into RESULTS.md and results.json)
analysis.estimator: ratio of paired sums - 1 (cost, calls, wall); mean paired difference (pass)
analysis.bootstrap: Rao-Wu rescaled bootstrap, stratified by family, clustered by variant: from each family's n_h variants draw m_h = n_h - 1 with replacement (both repeats of a variant together), weight n_h/m_h; percentile interval
analysis.why_rao_wu: with 8 clusters per stratum the naive percentile bootstrap under-covers; on plasmode data with a known truth the Rao-Wu interval covered 0.89 pooled and 0.875 per family (power.json ci90_coverage_known_truth), against 0.885 pooled for the naive percentile interval
analysis.pairs: complete (variant, repeat) pairs with both sessions ok or censored; infra and scorer errors are re-run by the runner's resume and never analysed; their cost stays in the spend
analysis.families_are_fixed: the CI is conditional on these 5 families (strata), not a sample of all possible families: it states the uncertainty from variants and sessions, not from which families were chosen

power.method: plasmode simulation (analyze.py --power, power.json): the 36 real card-vs-control pairs of the recurring-workflows research (calibration.json: click-type, mm-validator, go-flag; Haiku 4.5), each family's card effect removed, variants resampled with their repeats; a card effect applied to the variants the card reaches (75% of variants, as the GO dry run's 5/8-8/8 detection suggests), family effects varying with sd 6 points, no effect elsewhere; 200 datasets x 1,000 resamples per design
power.chosen_design: 5 families x 8 held-out variants x 2 repeats (160 held-out sessions)
power.what_it_buys: About $51 of Haiku sessions buys a pooled 90% interval of about +/-4.9 points (P(<=6) = 0.935): a true card effect of -20% (about 15% ITT) excludes 0 99.5% of the time, and one of -10% 78% of the time. It does NOT buy per-family precision: each family's interval is about +/-10 points, so per-family numbers are descriptive and a family-level saving under ~10% will often not exclude 0. One repeat instead of two (5x8x1, about $22 less) would widen the pooled interval to +/-6.7 (P(<=6) = 0.24). Ten held-out variants per family (5x10x2, 14 variants each, about $11 more) would reach P(<=6) = 0.99 but exceeds the $60 aim. The Sonnet arm's ~$7 buys a directional number (+/-12 points), not a precise one.

go-flag.basis: confirmation live: control $0.347 (6/12 hit 60 turns), card $0.230

http-header.basis: data-expansion http bug fixes $0.481 (HeaderMap internals, 6 sessions); a header constant is a smaller edit but compiles the crate several times; bytes $0.329

chi-middleware.basis: data-expansion chi bug fixes $0.214 (10 sessions); families cost 1.0-1.5x their repository's bug fixes

budget.sonnet_basis: Claude Sonnet 5 is $2/$10 per MTok against Haiku 4.5's $1/$5 (2x per token); stronger models use fewer turns (research: Sonnet-class agents avoid most procedural waste): assumed 0.7x the tokens, so 1.4x the $
budget.note: The global cap is hard: sc_run.py sums the spend recorded in every showcase root before each --execute and clamps each runner's cap to what remains. At the pessimistic factor the Haiku stages alone would exceed it; the stage order (every family's repeat 1 before any repeat 2, Sonnet last) makes a binding cap cost repeats and the Sonnet arm, never whole families.

stopping_rules.R1: global cap $60 across every showcase root: before each --execute, gv_run.py sums the spend recorded in all 7 roots, refuses once it reaches $60, and clamps the runner's cap (checked before every session) to what remains; per-root caps as budget.caps_usd. Sessions in flight when a cap is reached finish (at most 2, about $0.8)
stopping_rules.R2: after training (stage A), per family: if the learner did not run (learner-waits.jsonl shows a timeout, or learn.log is empty), that is infrastructure: fix and re-run the family's training in a fresh root (the first root's spend stays in the ledger). If the learner ran and formed no card, that is the product's behaviour: the family continues to held out (ITT) and is reported as 'no card formed'
stopping_rules.R3: the $0 probe (sc_detect.py) is REPORTED, never a stop: detection misses are part of what the shipped product does; its delivered_tasks fix the pre-treatment delivered subset
stopping_rules.R4: interim, after stage B (repeat 1 of all 5 families; `analyze.py --interim`, exit 4 = stop): stop for harm if adage has >= 5 fewer passes than control over the repeat-1 pairs, OR the pooled $/task is > +15% with its 90% CI lower bound > 0. No stopping for efficacy. Calibrated on plasmode data before any session (synthetic.json): false stop 0.01 under a true null and 0.05 at a true -20%; stops 0.485 / 0.74 of the time under a 25 / 35-point pass loss and 0.77 under a +25% cost harm. If R4 stops, stages C and D do not run and the report is the repeat-1 analysis, labelled interim-stopped-for-harm
stopping_rules.R5: infrastructure (disk full, auth or rate limits, container restart): pause and resume the same root; affected sessions are re-run by the runner's resume, their cost stays in the ledger
stopping_rules.R6: the Sonnet arm (stage D) starts only after stage C, and only if at least half its central estimate remains under the global cap (config min_remaining_usd); if the cap stops it part-way, it is reported with the pairs it has, labelled incomplete
stopping_rules.R7: no family, variant, arm or session is dropped, added or re-run for its outcome; the only re-runs are infrastructure errors (R5) and a learner that did not run (R2)

reporting.outputs: render.py -> RESULTS.md and results.json (schema adage-showcase-results/1), from analysis.json; only the quantities defined here
reporting.headline_rule: The headline states the primary with its 90% CI, n pairs, n variants, n families and the model. Wording by the CI alone: upper bound < 0 -> 'Adage cut the cost per task by X%'; lower bound > 0 -> 'Adage raised the cost per task by X%'; otherwise -> 'no detectable change in cost per task (X%)'. The same rule words every secondary and every per-family number.
always_reported: pass rate per arm and its paired difference
card delivery rate and false fires
total spend, including training, infrastructure re-runs and the Sonnet arm
reporting.per_family_rule: per-family numbers are reported with their intervals and the note that each rests on 8 variants (interval coverage about 88%); no family is singled out as the headline
reporting.sonnet_rule: the Sonnet arm is reported as directional (12 pairs, about +/-12 points), with the note that it used the Haiku-learned index
reporting.incomplete_rule: if any stage did not complete, the report says which, reports what completed, and the status field is 'incomplete' or 'interim-stopped-for-harm'
caveats_preregistered: Families, prompts, hidden checks and gold patches were written by the Adage team; prompts follow one template per family, and the shipped detector recognises near-template prompts, not informal paraphrases (0/6 in the Go research family).
The Adage arm's saving is intention-to-treat: sessions whose prompt the detector missed count, at no saving.
Learning was frozen during held-out sessions; a user's index would keep learning from them.
Each family rests on 8 held-out variants; per-family intervals are about +/-10 points and cover about 88% of the time.
The pooled figure weights families by their cost; the interval is conditional on these 5 families.
Wall time was measured on a shared machine.
The Sonnet arm is small (12 pairs) and used cards learned from Haiku sessions.
The go-flag family's CI requires an approval step (testdata/godoc-v3.x.txt) that no research training session performed; a card only repeats what earlier sessions did.

predictions.usd: pooled ITT -10% to -20% (research: -18.8% CLAUDE.md card on click+marshmallow, -33.8% hook card on Go; the release binary delivered the GO family's card for 8/8 held-out prompts in its dry run); with chi-middleware at ~0 (no card), the pooled ITT prediction is -8% to -16%
predictions.card_delivery: >= 75% of adage held-out sessions in the 4 carded families; 0 in chi-middleware; so >= 60% pooled
predictions.false_fires: about 3 of 30, all at the first edit of a card file on same-file fixes (dry run); 0 at the prompt
predictions.by_family: with this binary: no card and ~0 effect on chi-middleware (dry-run finding); the largest savings on go-flag; the smallest of the carded families on http-header (the compile loop dominates and repeats in both arms)
predictions.sonnet: a smaller relative saving than Haiku (stronger models waste less on procedure)

The product joins traces when prompts are similar (cosine >= 0.6) AND the shapes of their edited files overlap (Jaccard >= 0.25), a file's shape being (directory, name-token count, first token, extension). chi names each middleware's files after it (no_sniff.go, allow_methods.go, hsts.go, require_header.go), so only README.md is shared: Jaccard 0.2. Real sessions will name files the same way (upstream does), so the prediction is no card for this family with this binary

implications: chi-middleware is kept, unchanged: the family was fixed before the dry run, and dropping or renaming it because the product misses it would select families to suit the product. With this binary it is predicted to contribute ~0 to the pooled ITT (about 1/6 of the pooled cost weight) and to cost ~$8.4 for that. A product fix to the file-shape rule, if it lands before the live run, is used only under product.binary_rule (a new dry run recorded here first)

the grey-zone file signal (card at the first edit of a card file) works in this binary (it was broken in the GO validation's card-branch build) and fired on 3 of the 12 same-file negatives: false fires are defined to include it, and the prompt/edit split is reported
